title: The Seven Chakras and Their Stones
description: A clear guide to the seven chakras with each one's location, color and traditional themes, plus the crystals most often paired with every energy centre.
html:
The word chakra comes from Sanskrit and means wheel or disc. In traditions rooted in India, chakras are described as spinning centres of energy running along the spine, each connected with particular themes of life and feeling. Modern crystal practice borrows this map and pairs each centre with a color, then chooses stones of a matching or complementary color to work with. Whether you see the chakras as literal energy centres or as a useful framework for reflection, the system gives a clear, memorable way to organise your stones and your meditations.

Below you will find the seven main chakras from the base of the spine to the crown of the head. For each, we give the location, color, traditional themes and the stones most often used. Everything here reflects tradition and belief, and is meant to support relaxation and reflection.

How the system works

Most practitioners follow a few simple ideas:

  • Each chakra has a color from the rainbow, running from red at the base to violet at the crown.
  • Stones matching that color are said to resonate with the chakra.
  • A chakra is described as open and balanced, underactive or overactive. Crystal work aims at a sense of balance.
  • You can lie down with stones placed on the body, wear them as jewelry or simply hold one during meditation.

Root Chakra

Location: base of the spine, the pelvic floor.

Color: red.

Sanskrit name: Muladhara.

The root chakra is associated with stability, safety, belonging and the physical world. Practitioners connect it with feeling secure at home, steady with money and comfortable in the body. When people feel anxious, scattered or unsupported, they often say their root is out of balance.

Stones: Red Jasper, Garnet, Hematite, Black Tourmaline, Smoky Quartz and Obsidian. Red and black stones are used for grounding. Place one at the base of the spine while lying down, or hold it with bare feet on the floor.

Sacral Chakra

Location: lower abdomen, a few finger-widths below the navel.

Color: orange.

Sanskrit name: Svadhisthana.

The sacral chakra is tied to creativity, pleasure, emotional flow and relationships. Tradition says it governs how freely we feel, create and enjoy. People turn to it when they feel stuck, creatively blocked or disconnected from joy.

Stones: Carnelian, Sunstone, Orange Calcite, Peach Moonstone and Tangerine Quartz. These warm, glowing stones are often chosen for creative sessions, dancing, art and playful rituals. Orange Calcite is soft, so keep it dry.

Solar Plexus Chakra

Location: upper abdomen, between the navel and the base of the ribs.

Color: yellow.

Sanskrit name: Manipura.

The solar plexus is the seat of personal power, confidence, will and self-esteem. Practitioners link it to motivation and the ability to say no. It is the centre people call on before a job interview, a presentation or a big decision.

Stones: Citrine, Tiger's Eye, Yellow Jasper, Amber and Pyrite. Citrine and Tiger's Eye are the most popular, used for confidence and a steady sense of purpose. Pyrite looks like a lump of gold and carries a reputation for assertiveness and abundance, but it is brittle and should stay dry.

Heart Chakra

Location: centre of the chest.

Color: green (with pink as a secondary color).

Sanskrit name: Anahata.

The heart chakra is the bridge between the lower three centres, which deal with the self and the body, and the upper three, which deal with expression and spirit. It is associated with love, compassion, forgiveness, grief and the way we connect with others. Many practitioners work here when they feel closed off, lonely or tender after a loss.

Stones: Rose Quartz, Green Aventurine, Rhodonite, Emerald, Peridot, Rhodochrosite and Pink Tourmaline. Rose Quartz is the stone of unconditional love, while Green Aventurine suits a calm, optimistic heart. Place one over the breastbone and breathe slowly for several minutes.

Throat Chakra

Location: the base of the neck and throat.

Color: light blue.

Sanskrit name: Vishuddha.

The throat chakra is linked to communication, honesty, self-expression and listening. Singers, teachers and speakers have long been drawn to it. If you feel tongue-tied, or struggle to say what you mean, tradition suggests working here.

Stones: Blue Lace Agate, Aquamarine, Sodalite, Angelite, Larimar and Blue Calcite. Blue Lace Agate has a soft, banded pattern that many describe as soothing, and a pendant sits conveniently at the throat. Angelite is soft and sensitive to water.

Third Eye Chakra

Location: the forehead, between and slightly above the eyebrows.

Color: indigo.

Sanskrit name: Ajna.

The third eye is connected with intuition, imagination, insight and dreams. Traditions describe it as the centre of inner sight. Practitioners work here for meditation, dream recall, creative visualisation and a quiet mind.

Stones: Amethyst, Lapis Lazuli, Labradorite, Iolite, Sodalite and Fluorite. Lapis has been prized since antiquity for its deep blue and golden flecks. To use these stones, lie down and place one on the forehead for a short meditation, or keep amethyst beside the bed.

Crown Chakra

Location: the top of the head.

Color: violet or white.

Sanskrit name: Sahasrara.

The crown chakra is the point of connection with something larger than ourselves, whether you call it spirit, the universe or simply a sense of meaning. It is linked to spiritual growth, peace, awareness and trust. Practitioners turn to it for quiet contemplation.

Stones: Clear Quartz, Selenite, Amethyst, Howlite, Danburite and Herkimer Diamond. Clear, white and violet stones are placed above the head or held lightly in the hands during meditation. Selenite wands are a favourite because their pale glow suits quiet reflection.

Chakras beyond the seven

Many modern practitioners speak of extra points. The Earth Star sits below the feet and is paired with dark grounding stones, while the Soul Star sits above the crown and is paired with high-vibration clear stones such as Phenakite and Moldavite. These are newer additions and not part of the classic seven, so treat them as optional.

A simple chakra layout

For a full session, lie on your back and place a stone on each centre from root to crown, using one stone per chakra: Red Jasper, Carnelian, Citrine, Rose Quartz, Blue Lace Agate, Amethyst and Clear Quartz. Rest for ten to fifteen minutes with slow breathing, then remove the stones from crown to root and sit up gently. Stones must be clean and dry, since some of these are soft or sensitive. You can learn more about preparing them in our cleansing guide, or arrange them in a pattern using the crystal grid guide.

Colors are a starting point, not a rule. If a stone of the wrong color feels right on a particular chakra, follow your instinct. The system exists to help you pay attention.

Chakra work is a spiritual and relaxation practice, and crystals complement but never replace professional medical care.
